findings.reason: naming `cache_guard` as the counting owner reuses a measured instrument and removes the risk of a second, drift-prone compilation counter, which is the reuse defect this item exists to catch.
findings.text: §4's acceptance ("one compiled program serves two geometries of the same shape, counted as compilations") and §6's "compiled programs per mesh shape: one" propose a compile-count gate but name no instrument, while `scripts/h200_test_lane/cache_guard.py` already prints one row per program with its compile seconds and hit/miss outcome, so a two-geometry run with the cache disabled reports exactly the count the clause needs; the plan searched the solve machinery thoroughly but not the compile-counting surface, so a node may build a parallel counter

findings.text: the receipts-out-of-git decision routes npz/gz/json receipts above a few MB to a hardcoded `/work/projects/imas_gpu` root with "a path pointer in the evidence fragment", but names no owner for that placement; `nova/database/filepath.py` (`FilePath@134`) is the repository's path-resolution owner, and the GPFS literal already appears hardcoded in `nova/imas/mast_fitted_parameters.py:50`, `nova/catalog/mast_geometry.py:35`, `nova/media/sources/nova_labels.py:41` and other call sites

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the design hides the read, the booking, the map and its tangent, and the Newton solve behind four small signatures (`topology.read`, `current.book`, `gs.apply`, `solve.fixed_point`), each carrying substantial behaviour (sub-cell axis-connected membership, exact-clip moments, the differentiated composed map, Newton-GMRES under a scan); the retained `forward.py` facade is a declared adapter, not a fifth behaviour.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the receipts-out-of-git decision adds a large-artifact placement convention (hardcoded GPFS root under `/work/projects/imas_gpu` with a path pointer in the evidence fragment) without naming the path-resolution owner the codebase already uses, `nova/database/filepath.py` (`FilePath@134`); the same literal is already re-hardcoded in ~10 modules.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — the supplied figures are public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; the plan adds no reckon interface surface, and §6's request-surface ruling names what it retires from `ForwardSolvePolicy` (route, clip modes, the eight plumbing fields) and states the before/after field counts, satisfying the retire-or-justify rule for the one family it does touch.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan searched the solver, booking, topology, moment, operand and null machinery exhaustively and cites real symbols (verified: `fixed_point.py` `_single_site_krylov`@2619, `_backtracking_scores`@1270, `_select_backtracking_candidate`@1147, `_backtracked_promotion`@1333, `picard`@2874, `newton_krylov`@5003; `polygon_moments.py`; `contour_tree.py`; `constraint.py`; `domain.py`), but it proposes a compile-cost acceptance that is counted by no cited instrument, while the counting instrument already exists at `scripts/h200_test_lane/cache_guard.py`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the plan states in its own text that `gs.apply` replays the map `ForwardFluxOperator` performs "rather than wrapping it", that `topology.read` replaces `Topology.read`/`ForwardFluxOperator.read` in place, and that the retained single-site GMRES and backtracking helpers move into `solve.py` as private helpers behind one call site; each carry-or-decline ruling gives the reason, so no wrapper is added without justification.
